back: A region in which a moving charge, a current-carrying conductor or a magnetic pole experiences a force.

front: Field of a long straight wire
back: Concentric circles round the wire, further apart with distance; right-hand grip rule gives the direction.
Uniform inside (parallel, equally spaced lines along the axis); bar-magnet pattern outside.
Wire: thumb along current, fingers show field. Coil: fingers with current, thumb shows field inside (north end).
Same-direction currents attract; opposite currents repel; the forces are equal and opposite (third-law pair).
Greatly increases B and loses its magnetism when the current stops, so it suits electromagnets and relays.
Earth's field: a few × 10⁻⁵ T; fridge magnet: about 10⁻² T; MRI: 1.5 T or more.
Wire: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$; solenoid: $B = \mu_0 nI$; $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \text{H m}^{-1}$
